name: West and South Sikkim
tagline: Kangchenjunga views, Sikkim's first capitals and the great pilgrim statues
summary: West and South Sikkim cover the old West and South districts (now Gyalshing, Soreng and Namchi districts): Pelling, Yuksom, Rinchenpong, Ravangla and Namchi. Go for the closest town views of Kangchenjunga, the monasteries and ruins where the Sikkimese kingdom began, and the Goecha La trek. October to May is the time to go, with October, November, March and April best.
meta_description: West and South Sikkim travel guide: Pelling, Yuksom, Ravangla, Namchi, Rinchenpong. Best months, costs, permits, routes from Siliguri and trip plans.
intro: On this site West Sikkim means the whole western and southern half of the state. That is the old West Sikkim and South Sikkim districts, which since 2021 have become Gyalshing, Soreng and Namchi districts. The area runs from the Rangeet river near Jorethang up to the glaciers of Kangchenjunga, and its towns sit on ridges between 1,300 m and 2,200 m facing the highest part of the range.

It is where the Sikkimese kingdom began. Three lamas crowned the first Chogyal at Yuksom in 1642, the court moved to Rabdentse near Pelling in 1670, and the great monasteries of Pemayangtse, Sangachoeling, Dubdi and Tashiding were founded within a few decades. The sacred lakes of Khecheopalri and Kathok are part of the same landscape.

The south is greener, lower and more recent in its fame. Namchi and Ravangla now hold some of the largest statues in the Himalaya, Samdruptse's Guru Rinpoche and Ravangla's Buddha, along with Char Dham, while Temi Tea Garden covers the slopes towards the Teesta.

Indians need no permits anywhere in the region except for treks inside Khangchendzonga National Park. Distances are short, roads are mostly good, and the region pairs easily with Gangtok or Darjeeling.

highlights.title: Kangchenjunga from Pelling and Rinchenpong
highlights.text: Some of the closest and widest town views of the world's third-highest mountain, best at sunrise from October to April.

highlights.title: The first capitals of Sikkim
highlights.text: The coronation throne at Yuksom and the ruined palace at Rabdentse tell the story of the Namgyal kings from 1642.

highlights.title: Old monasteries
highlights.text: Pemayangtse, Sangachoeling, Dubdi, Tashiding and Rinchenpong are among the oldest Buddhist sites in Sikkim.

highlights.title: The great statues
highlights.text: Guru Rinpoche at Samdruptse, the Buddha at Ravangla and Shiva at Char Dham draw pilgrims from across India.

highlights.title: The Goecha La trek
highlights.text: Yuksom is the starting point for Dzongri and Goecha La, the best-known trek in Sikkim.

highlights.title: Farmstays and tea
highlights.text: Orange orchards and cardamom groves around Rinchenpong, and Sikkim's only tea estate at Temi.

facts: Nepali, Sikkimese (Bhutia), Lepcha, Limbu, Hindi, English
None for Indians; ILP for foreigners; park permits for treks
people: West and South Sikkim are home to Nepali-speaking communities, among them Limbu, Rai, Gurung, Tamang, Chettri and Bahun families, alongside Bhutia and Lepcha people who have lived here for centuries. The Bhutias brought Tibetan Buddhism, and the monasteries of Pemayangtse and Tashiding are still at the centre of their religious life. The Lepchas, Sikkim's earliest known people, keep their own language and their reverence for Tendong Hill and Kangchenjunga. Many families are Hindu, and Christianity is followed by some. Most people farm cardamom, ginger, oranges, maize and rice, and tourism now supports many homes. Nepali is the shared language; English is widely understood in towns.

months.summary: Some of the clearest mountain views of the year, with cold nights and frost. Crowds are thin after New Year and room rates fall.
months.tip: Ask for a heater and carry a down jacket for sunrise.

months.summary: Clear skies continue and days warm slowly. Losar, the Tibetan New Year, falls in February or March, and Bumchu at Tashiding often falls in this month.
months.tip: Check the Tibetan calendar for Bumchu dates and book Yuksom rooms early.

months.weather: Mild days, cool nights, 7–17°C in Pelling
months.summary: Rhododendrons begin to flower on the higher slopes and the first flush is plucked at Temi. Haze can build later in the month.
months.tip: Go out for views in the first hours after sunrise.

months.summary: Spring trekking season on the Goecha La trail, with rhododendrons in full bloom. Afternoon showers start to appear.
months.tip: Book Goecha La treks months ahead for April.

months.summary: Pleasant weather and green hills, but views are hazier and pre-monsoon storms arrive in the afternoon. School holidays bring families.
months.tip: Carry a rain jacket and plan outdoor visits for the morning.

months.summary: Rain sets in, the treks close and landslides start to affect roads. Hotels drop prices sharply.
months.tip: Keep a spare day and check road status each morning.

months.summary: The wettest month, with frequent landslides and little chance of seeing the range. Waterfalls are at their fullest.
months.tip: Travel only with a flexible plan and good rain gear.

months.summary: Monsoon continues. Lepcha communities mark Tendong Lho Rum Faat on 8 August, and Pang Lhabsol may fall late in the month.
months.tip: Allow extra hours on every drive.

months.summary: The monsoon thins out late in the month and the hills are very green. Pang Lhabsol at Ravangla often falls in September.
months.tip: Late September can bring the first clear mornings; stay flexible.

months.summary: The best month for views and trekking, and the busiest for hotels during the Puja holidays. Goecha La treks run at full capacity.
months.tip: Book rooms and cars well ahead for the Durga Puja and Diwali weeks.

months.summary: Excellent, stable weather and fewer crowds after Diwali. Oranges ripen around Rinchenpong late in the month.
months.tip: This is the sweet spot for clear views and fair prices.

months.summary: Sharp, clear mornings and cold nights. Ralang holds its masked dances, and Christmas to New Year is busy in Pelling.
months.tip: Book late-December rooms early, or come in the first half of the month.

getting_there: Bagdogra airport (IXB) and New Jalpaiguri station (NJP) near Siliguri are the gateways. From Siliguri the road follows the Teesta to Melli, where it splits: Namchi is about 100 km and 3.5–4 hours away, Ravangla about 120 km and 4.5–5 hours, Pelling about 135 km and 5–6 hours via Jorethang and Legship, Rinchenpong about 130 km and 5 hours, and Yuksom about 160 km and 6–7 hours. Shared jeeps leave Siliguri for Jorethang, Namchi, Gyalshing and Pelling each morning. From Gangtok, Ravangla is about 65 km and Pelling about 115–130 km. Darjeeling is about 75 km from Pelling via Jorethang. The NH10 along the Teesta is prone to landslides; check current status before you travel.
permits: Indian citizens need no permit to visit Pelling, Yuksom, Ravangla, Namchi or Rinchenpong; carry photo ID for hotels. Foreign nationals need the Sikkim Inner Line Permit (ILP), issued free at the Melli and Rangpo checkposts, in Siliguri and online, with passport and visa. Treks into Khangchendzonga National Park, such as Dzongri and Goecha La from Yuksom, need park entry permits and a registered guide for everyone; foreigners must also go through a registered Sikkim agency, usually in a group of two or more. Rules and fees change. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What does West Sikkim cover on this site
faqs.a: We use West Sikkim for the western and southern half of the state: the old West and South Sikkim districts, now Gyalshing, Soreng and Namchi districts. That includes Pelling, Yuksom, Rinchenpong, Ravangla and Namchi, with Tashiding, Khecheopalri Lake, Temi Tea Garden, Samdruptse and Char Dham covered under the nearest town.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for West and South Sikkim
faqs.a: Allow four to seven days. Three nights covers Pelling and Yuksom; five nights adds Namchi, Ravangla and Rinchenpong at an easy pace; seven nights lets you combine the region with Gangtok or Darjeeling. Treks from Yuksom need extra days: four to five for Dzongri, eight to ten for Goecha La.

faqs.q: Which is the best base in West Sikkim
faqs.a: Pelling is the most practical base, with the most hotels, the best-known view of Kangchenjunga and day trips to Khecheopalri Lake, Yuksom and Rinchenpong. Namchi and Ravangla work better as bases for the south. Rinchenpong suits a quiet stay. Most visitors split their nights between two or three places.

faqs.q: Do Indians need any permit for West Sikkim
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens need no permit for any town or village in West and South Sikkim. Carry a government photo ID for hotels. A permit is needed only for treks inside Khangchendzonga National Park, such as Dzongri and Goecha La, arranged in Yuksom with a registered guide. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit West Sikkim
faqs.a: October to early December gives the clearest views and dry roads, with October the busiest month. February to April brings flowers and good mornings, and April is spring trekking season. January is cold and very clear. June to September is monsoon, with rain, landslides and few views, though prices are lowest.

faqs.q: How do I get to Pelling from Bagdogra or NJP
faqs.a: Pelling is about 135–145 km from NJP and Bagdogra, 5–6 hours by road via Melli, Jorethang and Legship. A reserved small car costs about ₹5,000–6,500. Shared jeeps for Gyalshing and Pelling leave Siliguri each morning for about ₹400–500 a seat. Fares are indicative and rise in peak season.

faqs.q: Is West Sikkim good for a family trip
faqs.a: Yes. Altitudes are moderate, between about 1,300 m and 2,200 m, drives are mostly under 5 hours, and the main sights need little walking. Namchi and Ravangla have large, easy pilgrim parks, and Pelling has views from hotel rooftops. Bring warm clothes, as nights are cold from November to March.

faqs.q: How much does a West Sikkim trip cost per day
faqs.a: Indicatively, budget travellers spend about ₹1,800–2,800 per person a day using homestays and shared jeeps. Value travellers spend about ₹3,500–5,500 with good hotels and a private car shared by two. Comfort trips cost about ₹7,000–12,000. Cars are the biggest cost, so groups of four save the most.

faqs.q: Can I combine West Sikkim with Darjeeling
faqs.a: Yes, easily. Pelling to Darjeeling is about 75 km and 3.5–4.5 hours via Jorethang, and Rinchenpong to Darjeeling about 4 hours. Many travellers do Gangtok, Ravangla and Pelling, then finish in Darjeeling before flying from Bagdogra. Sikkim taxis can drop you in Darjeeling but usually cannot do local sightseeing there.
